paragraphs: Aristotle sells software, data, and consulting to political campaigns, political action committees, and advocacy groups. Its campaign management product, Campaign Manager, is cloud-based and covers compliance, fundraising, and accounting reporting. The firm also sells voter and consumer data to campaigns, PACs, corporations, and advocacy organizations in the United States and abroad.

The compliance practice files campaign finance, lobbying, pay-to-play, and Foreign Agent Registration Act reports federally, in 49 of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. That team of attorneys and paralegals is described as assisting over 230 clients with campaign finance, lobbying, and government ethics compliance. A division called Integrity sells identity and age verification products to commercial and government buyers. Overseas, the company says it has worked with candidates and political parties from Afghanistan to Ukraine and Kenya to Georgia.

Two brothers started the firm in 1983 to build what they described as the first campaign finance and reporting database. It is headquartered on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC. Compliance services are led by a former two-term Federal Election Commission chairman. The company claims that over more than 40 years almost every U.S. president has used its solutions, along with senatorial and congressional campaigns and state party initiatives from both major parties. It presents itself as a non-partisan provider open to members of all parties.
